module_title: File Extensions - Foundational Basics and MS Office Formats
introduction: How does an operating system know whether to open a file in MS Word or MS Excel? It relies on the 'File Extension'. An extension is the 3 or 4-letter suffix that appears after the period (dot) at the end of a file name. Identifying standard MS Office extensions is a guaranteed Tier-1 exam question.

core_concepts.title: MS Word Extensions (.doc and .docx)
core_concepts.description: The standard extension for MS Word document files. Up to Word 2003, the extension was strictly `.doc`. From Word 2007 onwards, Microsoft updated it to `.docx`.

core_concepts.title: MS Excel Extensions (.xls and .xlsx)
core_concepts.description: The standard extension for MS Excel spreadsheet/workbook files. In older legacy versions, it was `.xls`. Modern versions (2007 to present) use `.xlsx`.

core_concepts.title: MS PowerPoint Extensions (.ppt and .pptx)
core_concepts.description: The standard extension for MS PowerPoint presentation files. Legacy versions used `.ppt`, while modern versions use `.pptx`.

core_concepts.title: The Meaning of the 'x'
core_concepts.description: A highly tested fact: The 'x' added at the end of all modern MS Office extensions (post-2007) stands for **XML (Extensible Markup Language)**. This transition made Office files significantly smaller in size (compressed) and far less prone to corruption.

important_entities.name: File Extension Purpose
important_entities.significance: An extension's sole purpose is to instruct the Windows Operating System on exactly which default software program it should use to read and open that specific file.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Aspirants assume old and new files work identically everywhere. Note this rule: A modern MS Word 2019 software CAN easily open an old `.doc` file. However, an old MS Word 2003 software CANNOT open a modern `.docx` file without special converter plugins.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Doc = Document, XLS = eXceL Spreadsheet, PPT = PowerPoint
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: The first three letters of the extension almost always directly spell out the name or primary function of the software.

exam_strategy_tips: In SSC preliminary exams, you will often be asked: 'What is the default file extension of MS Excel 2010?' Always select the option ending in 'x' (i.e., `.xlsx`).
